videos.script: A container that is up is not the same as a program that works. This lesson is about three things around the program. {{logs}} First, logs. By default Docker keeps every line, forever. A program stuck in a loop wrote a hundred and eighty megabytes in three seconds. Two options keep that to three small files. {{health}} Then health checks. Docker runs a small command inside the container, and marks it healthy or not. A shelf listening on the wrong port looks fine to docker ps. The check catches it. {{secrets}} And last, secrets during a build. A token passed as a build argument ends up in the image's history. A secret mount does not.
